hero.title: Karunya Institute of Technology and Sciences
hero.summary: Karunya’s School of Agricultural Sciences in Coimbatore describes a substantial instructional farm, protected cultivation structures and subject divisions. It offers undergraduate agriculture and specialist postgraduate courses, with field experiments and entrepreneurship modules forming part of its published educational account.

overview.heading: Field-based agricultural study in Coimbatore
paragraphs: Karunya dates its School of Agricultural Sciences to 2017. The current school page describes eleven academic divisions, covering crop, soil, plant-health, engineering and allied subjects. Its farm and laboratory setting supports a programme account that extends beyond lecture teaching to crop experiments, protected cultivation and agricultural enterprise learning.

Official sources list a four-year B.Sc. Agriculture together with postgraduate agronomy, genetics and plant breeding, and fruit science. These subject options allow students to distinguish crop production, crop improvement and horticultural study. Entry wording differs between the academics page and the brochure located during research, so applicants need the definitive course notice before selecting a school-subject or postgraduate route.

admissions.heading: Planning an agriculture application
admissions.intro: The live official UG admissions page now describes the 2027 cycle. It states that KEE 2027 is mandatory for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture and that confirmation depends on the stated qualifying-examination requirements. Treat these as next-cycle instructions; the 2026–30 cohort fee sheet below remains explicitly labelled by its own source session. Older academic and brochure descriptions differ, so request the exact intake-year subject rules.

scholarships.heading: Scholarships and financial support
scholarships.text: Karunya’s 2026–27 scholarship page explicitly includes B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture in its Indian-student merit grid. The separate Founder’s Scholarship offers a limited 100% tuition waiver for eligible Indian Christian applicants; its 2026 application and selection dates have passed.

schemes.name: B.Sc. Agriculture Indian-student merit grid, 2026–27
schemes.details: The agriculture column lists INR 1,20,000 at 95% PCM/PCB, INR 60,000 at 90%, and INR 40,000 at 85%. These are scholarship amounts, not net tuition payable. Obtain the approved award and applicable continuation terms.
schemes.award: Agriculture-column amounts: INR 1,20,000 / 60,000 / 40,000 for the 95% / 90% / 85% bands.
schemes.eligibility: Indian applicants; specified Class 12 PCM/PCB marks and the approved award conditions.
schemes.renewal: No separately verified continuation rule is reproduced from this web grid.

schemes.name: Founder’s Scholarship 2026–27
schemes.details: Limited 100% tuition waiver for selected Indian Christian applicants with at least 90% PCM/PCB and annual family income below INR 8 lakh. Screening includes documentary verification and interview. The 29 May 2026 deadline is past.
schemes.award: 100% tuition waiver for selected eligible applicants; limited awards.
schemes.eligibility: Indian Christian applicant; agriculture threshold 90% PCM/PCB and family income below INR 8 lakh.
schemes.documents: Religion proof through TC/school-leaving or government community certificate; Form 16 AY 2025–26 or the specified competent-authority income certificate.

placements.heading: Career support and outcomes
placements.text: Karunya Institute of Technology and Sciences publishes an Agriculture and Allied Sectors submission for NIRF 2026. Its programme-duration cohorts report the graduating group, students placed, students entering higher studies and the median salary of placed graduates. These historical institutional submissions are not a placement promise or a salary estimate for every student or individual specialisation.

faqs.question: When did Karunya’s agriculture school begin?
faqs.answer: The school’s official page states 2017; that is the school date, not the university’s founding year.

faqs.question: Which agricultural programmes are listed?
faqs.answer: The current school page names B.Sc. Agriculture and master’s courses in agronomy, genetics and plant breeding, and fruit sciences.

faqs.question: Are protected-cultivation facilities documented?
faqs.answer: Yes. The school names polyhouses and mist chambers alongside research plots.

faqs.question: Does the checked ICAR entry accredit Karunya’s master’s programmes?
faqs.answer: The audited row prints only B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture. A broader website claim is unresolved and is not adopted here.

faqs.question: Is PCM alone definitely accepted?
faqs.answer: The academics page includes PCM, while the located brochure uses different biology/agriculture wording. Confirm the current intake rule directly.
